title: Choose the visual world for ashlyndrago.com
question: The roll assigned the Black-Paper Sketchbook. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Black-Paper Sketchbook
options.lineage: an artist's black-paper sketchbook, drawn in white and blue gel pen
options.thesis: The site is Ashlyn's own sketchbook: her photo taped in, her art pasted onto the spreads, her notes in blue ink.
options.viewport: One open spread on a gutter: her photo taped onto the left page, her name hand-set across the right page, with blue-ink notes ('actress', 'digital artist') and an index of pages.
options.risk: Reads as scrapbook-cute if the tape and notes multiply; it has to stay one disciplined object.

raised.raise: Fixed page grid: every spread uses the same margins and gutter, and only the pasted work changes.
Accent scarcity: blue ink is used only for Ashlyn's own marks (notes, links, the current page), never as decoration.
One dominant spread per screen. The gallery advances spread by spread instead of tiling into a card grid.

options.label: The Playbill
options.lineage: the theatre programme and its 'Who's Who in the Cast' page
options.thesis: Her portfolio as the programme for a show that hasn't opened yet. Art is the exhibit; the acting is the bio.
options.viewport: A midnight-blue masthead reading ASHLYN DRAGO in condensed caps, her photo as the cover image, and a 'Who's Who' bio column.
options.risk: The most familiar choice for an actress; it could read like a costume for credits she doesn't have yet.

options.label: Hand-Processed Film
options.lineage: 16mm film strip with sprockets, edge codes and light leaks
options.thesis: Each artwork is a frame on a strip, and her photo is the first exposed frame.
options.viewport: Her photo as frame 01 on a vertical strip, with stamped edge codes giving her name and roles.
options.case: Strong on actress identity, but weaker for showing digital art, which isn't film.
options.risk: Grain and light-leak effects can drift into a generic filter.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.thesis: Works as rows on a departure board.
options.risk: Cold and transit-y for a personal artist.
options.case: Ashlyn's audience doesn't connect with transit signage.
options.kept: A fixed grid where only the content changes.

options.label: ANSI Nightboard
options.thesis: The portfolio as a text-mode board.
options.risk: Retro gimmick that hides the art.
options.case: Text-mode chrome fights her painted work.
options.kept: Accent reserved for one meaning only.

options.label: Guide Map Lobes
options.thesis: Sections as lobes on a map.
options.viewport: A green lobe holding her photo.
options.case: Conflicts with the pinned palette, and the map metaphor is foreign to her.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.risk: Abstract; it says nothing about her.
options.case: No link to acting or digital art.
options.kept: One governing geometry for all alignment.

options.label: Du Bois Data Portraits
options.risk: Cream ground breaks the pinned dark palette, and it's a data form with no data.
options.case: No data to chart; the palette conflicts with the brief.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean dark portfolio: full-bleed photo hero, then a masonry art grid, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Her photo full-bleed with her name over it, and a navigation bar above.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other portfolio theme.
